notes: Perfect claim overlap (C39-C48). Both agree the context-dependent role of DNA methylation is well-supported, particularly the differential association of mQTLs to CGI vs non-CGI promoters. Peer reviewers explicitly state findings are 'intriguing and well supported' and 'otherwise satisfactory.'

Perfect claim overlap (C6, C59-C60, C68, C71-C73, C76-C77). Both express uncertainty about Bayesian Network causal inference. LLM cites inherent limitations of observational causality; peer reviewers question AIC correction adequacy and lack of significance evaluation via permutation testing. Both agree experimental validation needed.

Perfect claim overlap (C55-C58). LLM finds synergistic SNP-methylation interactions well-supported with appropriate statistical controls. Peer reviewers identify P-value inflation in Figure 3C and question whether controls adequately address confounding, requiring bootstrapping and additional corrections before accepting findings.

High claim overlap (C5, C50-C54; C49 only in LLM). LLM finds allele-specific expression analysis provides strong evidence that methylation doesn't drive ASE. Peer reviewers characterize this as 'a strong assertion, but also a negative result' and explicitly 'urge the authors to remove this result' unless additional support provided.

High claim overlap (C61-C67; C69-C70 only in peer review). LLM finds TF-methylation associations show strong enrichment with appropriate controls. Peer reviewers acknowledge 'intriguing and important direction' but question whether P-values are properly corrected and require permutation testing plus toned-down conclusions absent biological validation.

Moderate claim overlap (C33-C34, C36-C38 shared; C3, C31-C32 only in LLM; C4 only in peer). LLM supports enrichment of eQTMs/mQTLs at differentiated sites. Peer reviewers question whether relationship is artifact of average methylation variance and state 'biological conclusions are over-stretched and should be toned down.'

Partial overlap (C3, C31-C32 shared; LLM includes C33-C34, C36-C38; peer includes C75). LLM supports finding that developmental and inter-individual methylation operate through different mechanisms. Peer reviewers state conclusion about eQTM independence from repressive methylation is 'poorly supported' and may reflect 'artifact of binning' requiring finer analysis.

Minimal overlap (only C4 shared; LLM includes C35, C75). LLM supports conceptual claim that differentiation provides platform for inter-individual variation. Peer review R2 addresses C4 among other claims and states 'biological conclusions are over-stretched,' indicating interpretive claims exceed data support.

Minimal overlap (only C75 shared; LLM includes C4, C35). LLM supports finding about repressive methylation showing both positive/negative associations. Peer review R1 addresses C75 among other claims (C3, C31-C32) and questions whether binning approach masks true relationships.
Claims C24-C30 (experimental design, sample sizes, QC, statistical thresholds) only evaluated by LLM. No corresponding peer review assessment found. LLM finds methodology sound and rigorous.
